required_changes_injected: FAIL: Criterion 2 (Carry-forward consistency). Metrics scored 8/10 in cumulative state with evidence 'Scaling goals of 200 engineering users by end of 2026; cost per user at US$1,250/year'. Fresh analysis downgrades to 5/10 claiming the 200-user figure is 'capacity/adoption targets, not outcome metrics'. However, the justification for downgrade relies on re-interpreting the same May 20 call transcript that generated the prior 8/10 score. The analysis states 'The May 20 call transcript — which is the same underlying call that generated the prior summary — contains materially more detail than the first summary captured.' This is a reinterpretation of existing evidence, not new contradictory information from a subsequent call. Under Criterion 2, when cumulative_calls_context shows prior scoring on the same call, a downgrade requires documented new information from a different/later call, not a reanalysis of the same source. The score change log acknowledges this is the same call but justifies the downgrade as 'additional call detail contradicts the prior run's characterization.' This violates carry-forward rules: either the prior 8/10 was correct (maintain it) or it was incorrect (acknowledge the prior analysis was flawed, do not frame it as new information). Additionally, Decision Criteria scored 9/10 in cumulative state; fresh analysis downgrades to 7/10 claiming 'no formal written scorecard' was referenced. The cumulative evidence already stated 'Must-haves include query optimization, cost fields, and launch checklists; nice-to-haves involve advanced analytics and QA frameworks' — this same evidence is cited in the fresh analysis. A downgrade from 9/10 to 7/10 on the same evidence without new contradictory information violates carry-forward consistency. The analysis must either maintain prior scores with explicit 'No new information' statements, or cite new call evidence that contradicts the prior assessment.
